To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the emergence of 3D-stacking technology with memory and logic has brought about a renewed interest in “processing in-memory” (PIM), (2) the term PIM is often misused to describe a wide spectrum of in-memory computing, ranging from fully-programmable to fixed-function PIM architectures, and (3) fixed-function PIM is a viable option for many applications that can benefit from in-memory computing, but has not been adequately explored.

(i) PIM can be implemented with a wide range of compute capabilities, from simple logic gates to complex processing units, and (ii) there exists a case for exploring fixed-function compute capabilities in the memory stack.

“The emerging 3D-stacking technology has the potential to bring a renaissance in PIM, and the PIM concept should be studied in the context of fixed-function processing in addition to fully programmable PIM architectures.”.

understanding how we can best leverage the emerging memory stack for in-memory computing.
the design of memory architectures that can be used to accelerate computation in the datacenter.
understanding the potential of fixed-function PIM, and its role in the future of computing.

there is a wide spectrum of PIM capabilities that are possible, and that fixed-function PIM is an important part of the design space to be explored.
